name: Presentation (16:9)
note: Two kinds of slides. (1) Reference slides designed by the brand team in Figma (Design MCP › Layouts): kept as designed; only background colour, fonts, chips and logo placement are mapped to the design system. (2) Slides Claude designs: follow every guardrail below. Approved 2026-10-16.

safe_area.note: Every slide, including hero slides (page breaker, closing), aligns logo, labels, titles and content to the 52px edge. The Figma slides' 70px content guide and 134px hero inset are replaced (neither is on the spacing scale).

hero_title.use: page breaker and closing statements, big numbers

guardrails.note: Guidance for whoever designs in this format. user_decides = what is made (the user's call); fixed = do not change; must_not = hard limits; avoid = strong advice; design_direction = how to use the system; claude_decides = how it looks, where the designer has freedom. Every design item cites its basis in the design system.
user_decides: What is being made, for whom and why: the deck, its purpose and audience.
The content and facts. The designer uses exactly what the user supplies or approves: never invents, adds, rewrites, shortens or cuts it, and asks before suggesting a change.
The scope: which slides; nothing is added that was not asked for; when it is unclear, ask.
The number of slides, when the user sets it.
Whether an AI slide stays dark (Claude asks).
Which page-breaker or closing design to use, from the reference slides.

fixed.text: 52px padding on all four sides (spacing/52) on every slide, hero slides included: logo, labels, titles and content all align to it; content area 1816 × 976 px.
Text uses the named text style for its element (e.g. headline Display/LG Bold, body Body/24), between 14px and 72px.
Logo top-right on the 52px edge: white on dark and brand slides, blue on light; size may vary.
Delivered as an HTML file by default; PDF or PPTX only when the user asks for it.
Three themes: light (background/primary), dark (background/inverse) and brand (background/brand), each with its fixed text and logo colours.
Reference slides from Figma keep their design; only background colour, fonts, chips and logo placement are mapped to the design system.

must_not.text: Hard rule: never edit or change the user's content (no rewriting, shortening, cutting or adding). If a change seems needed, highlight it, suggest how it could be shown better, and change nothing unless the user approves.
Never let text overflow the canvas padding on any side, or the card, box, zone or node it sits in.
Never set text above 72px: the largest style is Display/XL (72/80), even for hero titles, closing statements and big numbers.
Never use a colour that is not a design-system token, and never sample or approximate one.
Never use a font other than TASA Orbiter (headings) and Inter (body).
Never use in-between font sizes: text comes from Role/* or the defined text styles.
Never put a pill radius on a card, panel, container, input or image.
Never place an eyebrow on container/secondary or container/tertiary (it fails contrast).
Never combine a shadow with a border of 2px or more.

avoid.text: Avoid using the accent colours (accent and accent-2 together) on more than roughly 10–15% of the piece; it is a highlight, not a palette.
Avoid text/tertiary for essential text; at 3.4:1 it is for large or non-essential text only.

design_direction.text: Slides about AI default to the dark theme; ask the user whether to keep it dark.
Highlight key words with text/link on light, text/accent on dark and text/accent-on-brand on brand slides, within the shared accent budget.

Start from the reference slides: product stack and team as designed; page breakers and closing slides from the hero designs; normal content from the content-slide references, adapted to the user's content.
Pick spacing by purpose: gap/inline between adjacent items, gap/stack inside a component, gap/grid between cards, padding/container inside cards, padding/section between sections.
Cards and panels use the container default: container/primary, 1px border/container, radius/default, padding/container. Nest with container/secondary, then container/tertiary.
Headings use text/heading, body copy text/body, eyebrows text/eyebrow.
Show status with the five intents (Positive, Negative, Information, Neutral, Primary) and their fixed fill/text pairs; warnings use Negative.
Keep surfaces flat; use Low Raised only to lift a card off the canvas.
Buttons have softened square corners (radius/default), never pill.
When an icon helps, use Lucide and colour it with a text token that suits the surface.
If the content is too much for the space, do not squeeze it below the minimum size or cut it: tell the user, and offer options (split across slides or pages, a different layout, a table or chart).

claude_decides: Layout and composition within the grid: what goes where, how many columns, what leads.
Visual hierarchy: what is large, what is quiet, and how the eye moves.
Which components to use and how to combine them, including arrangements nobody has drawn before.
How to show each idea: a stat, a process, a comparison, a story.
How the requested content is spread across slides (unless the user sets the number), and the single message of each slide.

overrides.reason: Matches the brand team's designed slides (small text and chart labels at 14px and up); decided 2026-10-16.

export.note: HTML by default; the user can ask for a PDF or PPTX version.

dark.note: Mapped from the designed slides' #132335 to the nearest token.

ai_slides.rule: Any slide about AI defaults to the dark theme, but ask the user whether to keep it dark before finishing.

reference_slides.source: Figma file Design MCP › Layouts page. The brand team keeps adding references: page breakers, closing slides, fixed slides (product stack, team) and content-slide layouts.
reference_slides.rule: Keep each reference slide's layout and decoration as designed. Map only: background colour to the theme token, fonts to the nearest text style (14–72px), chips to the chip tokens, and the logo to its design-system placement. For content references, Claude may adapt the layout to the content, still mapping these four.

mapping.background: theme background token (background/brand, background/inverse or background/primary)
mapping.fonts: nearest named text style, never below 14px or above 72px (Display/XL)
mapping.chips: container/inverse + text/inverse, radius/md, padding spacing/8 × spacing/12, Body/XL Semi Bold, uppercase text
mapping.logo: top-right on the 52px edge; white on dark and brand, blue on light; size may vary

product_stack.figma: 13 · Harness — every capability exposed to agents
product_stack.use: Whenever the product stack is asked for, use this slide as designed (only the mapping above).

team.use: Default for about or team slides, unless the user gives feedback.

page_breaker.use: One of the page-breaker designs; more will be added.

closing.use: One of the closing designs; more will be added.

content.figma: content layouts on the Layouts page (e.g. 14 · knowledge flywheel, 20 · customer journey, 23/24 · GTM, 26 · plan)
content.use: Starting points for normal content slides; more will be added.

kinds.fixed: product stack, team — used as designed whenever asked for
kinds.hero: page breakers and closing slides — pick one of the designs
kinds.content: layouts for normal content slides — a starting point Claude adapts to the user's content
